Iron-based materials including Fe, Fe₂O₃, Fe₃O₄, carbonyl iron, and FeO are used for EMI shielding due to their biocompatibility and biodegradability.
EMI shielding efficiency is defined as SE_T = 10log(P_I/P_T) = 20log(E_I/E_T) = 20log(H_I/H_T), where P, E, and H represent power and electric and magnetic field intensities.
Total shielding effectiveness is composed of three components: SE_T = SE_R + SE_A + SE_M.
Reflection loss formula: SE_R = 39.5 + 10log(σ/(2πfμ)) dB.
Absorption loss formula: SE_A = 8.7d√(fμσ) dB, where d is thickness.
Skin depth is calculated as δ = (fμσ)^(-1/2), representing the depth at which EM field is attenuated to 1/e of initial value.
Multiple reflection loss formula: SE_M = 20log(1 - e^(-2d/δ)) dB.
Attenuation constant: α = 4π√(3)/λ₀ for nonmagnetic materials and α = 4π(3μ)^(1/2)/λ₀ for magnetic materials.
Complex permittivity: ε = ε' + jε'', where ε' is energy storage capacity and ε'' relates to dielectric losses.
Complex permeability: μ = μ' + jμ'', where μ' is magnetic energy storage and μ'' relates to magnetic losses.
Impedance matching condition: Z_in = Z_0 = 377Ω for maximum microwave absorption.
Reflection loss at impedance matching: RL(dB) = 20log|(Z_in - Z_0)/(Z_in + Z_0)|.
Matching thickness formula: t_m = nc/(4f_m√(3μ)), where n is refractive index and c is velocity of light.
A minimum reflection loss of -20 dB is considered 99% microwave absorption.
Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles with size 20-30 nm show SE_Total of 68 dB compared to 47 dB for 10-20 nm particles.
Sample thickness variation from 0.1 mm to 0.7 mm enhances SE_T from 24 dB to 68 dB in Fe₃O₄/CF composites.
Snoek's limit: f_r(μ-1) ≤ fM_s, constraining permeability in ferromagnetic materials.
Natural resonance frequency: f_r = γH_a/(2π), where γ is gyromagnetic ratio and H_a is anisotropy field.
Anisotropy field: H_a = 2K/(μ₀M_s), where K is anisotropy constant and M_s is saturation magnetization.
Spin rotational susceptibility: K_sr = 2πM_s²/σ.
Domain wall motion susceptibility: K_dw = K_sr/(1 + j(ω/ω_sr)).
Percolation threshold conductivity: σ = σ₀(V - V_c)^c, where V is volume fraction and c is critical exponent.
Dielectric loss: ε'' = σ/(2πε₀f) for conductive materials.
Cole-Cole semicircle relationship: (ε_s - ε_N)² + (ε'')² = (ε_s - ε_N)², indicating Debye dipolar relaxation.
Heat treatment creates defects (vacancies, dangling bonds) that enhance attenuation rather than reflection in ferrite systems.
